PHRM 100.title: Foundations of Pharmacy
PHRM 100.description: Scientific concepts and pharmacy practice principles. Role of the pharmacist, patient assessment skills, professional identity, communication skills, and an understanding of legal and ethical responsibilities.

PHRM 111.title: Medication Management I
PHRM 111.description: Modules and integration activities focusing on: an introduction to infectious diseases; musculoskeletal disorders; dermatology; head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat disorders; and hematology.

PHRM 131.title: Study Design and Interpretation I
PHRM 131.description: Principles of clinical study design, focusing on biostatistical foundations, randomized controlled trials, and systematic review of randomized controlled trials.

PHRM 141.title: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice I
PHRM 141.description: Current and future roles for pharmacists and controversies in pharmacy practice.

PHRM 161.title: Technology in Healthcare
PHRM 161.description: Knowledge and skills related to the role and applications of technology in health care.

PHRM 171.title: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient I
PHRM 171.description: Direct patient care and drug distribution activities in an outpatient setting. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 171.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 100, PHRM_V 111, PHRM_V 131, PHRM_V 141, PHRM_V 161

PHRM 211.title: Medication Management II
PHRM 211.description: Modules and integration activities focusing on respirology and cardiovascular disorders.

PHRM 212.title: Medication Management III
PHRM 212.description: Modules and integration activities focusing on nephrology, endocrinology, and neurology.

PHRM 221.title: Nutrition for Pharmacists
PHRM 221.description: Foundations of nutrition, nutrition for healthy individuals through the lifespan, and selected clinical applications of nutrition in pharmacy practice.

PHRM 231.title: Study Design and Interpretation II
PHRM 231.description: Principles of screening and diagnostic tests, clinical prediction rules, clinical practice guidelines, conflicts of interest, economic evaluation of therapeutics and medical technologies, harm-benefit analysis, and how to incorporate the best available evidence into practice.

PHRM 241.title: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice II
PHRM 241.description: Current and future roles for pharmacists and controversies in pharmacy practice, focusing on the roles and training opportunities for pharmacists in specialty areas of outpatient and inpatient practice.

PHRM 251.title: Institutional Practice Skills
PHRM 251.description: Practice environment familiarization and skill development in preparation for experiential learning in inpatient and health authority-based settings.

PHRM 252.title: Clinical Skills: Administration of Injections
PHRM 252.description: Training for authorization to administer injections.

PHRM 261.title: Indigenous Health and Cultural Safety
PHRM 261.description: Overview of Indigenous health in Canada and the role a pharmacist can have in collaborating with Indigenous communities in providing culturally safe care and healing.

PHRM 270.title: Community Service Learning
PHRM 270.description: Service learning activities with external community partner sites and members. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 271.title: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient II
PHRM 271.description: Direct patient care and drug distribution activities in an outpatient setting, building pharmaceutical knowledge and problem-solving ability. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 271.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 211, PHRM_V 212, PHRM_V 221, PHRM_V 231, PHRM_V 241, PHRM_V 251, PHRM_V 252, PHRM_V 261, PHRM_V 270

PHRM 272.title: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Inpatient and Health Authority-Based
PHRM 272.description: Direct patient care activities in inpatient and other health authority-based settings, with application of foundational knowledge and skills. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 272.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 211, PHRM_V 212, PHRM_V 221, PHRM_V 231, PHRM_V 241, PHRM_V 251, PHRM_V 252, PHRM_V 261, PHRM_V 270

PHRM 302.title: Directed Studies in Clinical Pharmacy
PHRM 302.description: Individual assignments involving library and clinical investigation of specific problems relating to drug utilization and information topics.

PHRM 303.title: Directed Studies in Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
PHRM 303.description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation of problems involved in the development of pharmaceutical dosage forms.

PHRM 304.title: Directed Studies in Pharmacy Education
PHRM 304.description: Individual assignments involving library and scholarly inquiry related to pharmacy education.

PHRM 305.title: Directed Studies in Pharmacology
PHRM 305.description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation of certain aspects of drug action.

PHRM 306.title: Directed Studies in Pharmacy Practice
PHRM 306.description: Individual assignments involving library and field work investigations of problems associated with pharmacy practice.

PHRM 307.title: Directed Studies in Epidemiology and Health Outcomes
PHRM 307.description: Individual assignments involving scholarly inquiry related to epidemiology or health outcomes.

PHRM 311.title: Medication Management IV
PHRM 311.description: Modules and integration activities focusing on psychiatry, gastroenterology disorders, and oncology and palliative care.

PHRM 312.title: Medication Management V
PHRM 312.description: Modules and integration activities focusing on reproductive health, sexual health, and genitourinary disorders; special infectious diseases; and toxicology.

PHRM 321.title: Travel Health
PHRM 321.description: Providing a consultative service to patients based on patient medical and travel history. Recommending and administering vaccinations according to guidelines. Making recommendations regarding oral medications needed for safe travel.

PHRM 322.title: Peer Teaching in Pharmacy Skills
PHRM 322.description: Development and delivery of patient counselling role-playing activities.

PHRM 323.title: Pharmaceutical Care in Indigenous Health
PHRM 323.description: Indigenous health in Canada and the role pharmacists' cultural humility and safety can play when collaborating with other health professionals and Indigenous communities to provide care and healing.

PHRM 324.title: Primary Care Pharmacy Practice
PHRM 324.description: Strategies for leveraging opportunities and addressing barriers to effective pharmacist integration into multidisciplinary primary care teams and optimizing patient care.

PHRM 325.title: Clinical Pharmacokinetics
PHRM 325.description: Lectures and discussions of topics on the application of pharmacokinetic principles and the use of therapeutic drug level monitoring in clinical pharmacy practice.

PHRM 326.title: Renal Pharmacotherapeutics
PHRM 326.description: Case-based approach to pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical pharmacokinetics, and pharmacotherapy in nephrology with emphasis on the integration and application of fundamental principles to clinical situations in class.

PHRM 327.title: Precision Medicine
PHRM 327.description: Precision medicine approaches in research and medical practice to mitigate drug toxicity and improve drug efficacy.

PHRM 328.title: Pharmacology of Drugs of Misuse and Abuse
PHRM 328.description: Biological, pharmacological, and psychological aspects of drugs of misuse and abuse.

PHRM 329.title: Leadership Experience Applied to Pharmacy (LEAP)
PHRM 329.description: Leadership skills in preparation for the practice of pharmacy in direct or non-direct patient care settings and contexts.

PHRM 330.title: Pharmacy Practice in Acute and Critically Ill Patients
PHRM 330.description: Pharmaceutical care concepts for managing acute and critically ill patients.

children.raw: A combined average of 70% or higher in

PHRM 330.prerequisiteText: A combined average of 70% or higher in PHRM_V 211 and PHRM_V 212, and all of PHRM_V 271, PHRM_V 272

PHRM 331.title: Queering Health
PHRM 331.description: The historical and contemporary contexts of 2SLGBTQ+ health, the role of pharmacists, and select therapeutic topics related to 2SLGBTQ+ health.

PHRM 332.title: Practical Applications of Pharmacoepidemiology & Health Economics
PHRM 332.description: Principles and methods of collecting epidemiological and economic evidence used to assess the value of pharmaceuticals and services provided by pharmacists.

PHRM 333.title: Pharmacotherapy in Oncology
PHRM 333.description: Common oncological diseases and their drug treatment.

PHRM 334.title: Supporting Patients with Substance Use Disorders
PHRM 334.description: Substance use disorders and their treatment; the pharmacist's role in working with individuals who have a substance use disorder.

PHRM 340.title: Pain Research and Therapy
PHRM 340.description: Basic mechanisms and the clinical management of acute and chronic pain.

PHRM 341.title: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice III
PHRM 341.description: Current and potential roles for pharmacists, and contemporary issues in pharmacy practice. Focus on the role of pharmacists as patient educators, researchers and collaborators in interprofessional teams.

PHRM 346.title: Diabesity
PHRM 346.description: Current issues in obesity and diabetes from pathophysiology to patient care, with a focus on healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, and optimizing outcomes.

PHRM 351.title: Practice Management and Leadership
PHRM 351.description: Application of management and leadership principles and skills to pharmacy operations.

PHRM 371.title: Outpatient I Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHRM 371.description: Direct patient care activities in an outpatient setting, with increasing diversity of patient care situations. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 371.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 311, PHRM_V 312, PHRM_V 341, PHRM_V 351

PHRM 441.title: Seminar: Advanced Topics in Pharmacy Practice
PHRM 441.description: Pharmacists in practice, emerging pharmacy practice issues and pharmacists as preceptors. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 450.title: PharmD Seminar
PHRM 450.description: Seminar course about current and potential roles for pharmacists. Students will also deliver an individual and a group seminar. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 451.title: Critical Appraisal of Pharmacotherapy Literature
PHRM 451.description: Principles of clinical study design, focusing on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control), pharmacoeconomic analyses, clinical prediction rules, and guidelines. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 452.title: Patient Assessment Skills
PHRM 452.description: Principles and practices of patient assessment, applied to the monitoring of drug efficacy and toxicity. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 453.title: Applied Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacogenomics
PHRM 453.description: Pharmacokinetic monitoring of drug therapy in common clinical situations with foundations for application to other drugs. Pharmacogenomics and personalized medicine principles and applications to practice. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 454.title: Practice Management
PHRM 454.description: Values, concepts, issues and responsibilities of individuals exercising leadership and management roles in pharmacy practice and health care settings. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 462.title: Pharmacotherapeutics 2
PHRM 462.description: Respirology, dermatology, and ears, eyes, nose, and throat. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 467.title: Pharmacotherapeutics 7
PHRM 467.description: Genitourinary disorders, reproductive health, endocrinology, and nephrology. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 469.title: Pharmacotherapeutics 9
PHRM 469.description: Acute and critical care of nephrology, neurology, cardiovascular disorders, gastroenterology, infectious diseases, and respirology. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 471.title: Outpatient II Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHRM 471.description: Direct patient care activities in an outpatient setting, with increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a wide range of therapeutic areas. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 472.title: Inpatient and Health Authority-Based Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHRM 472.description: Direct patient care activities in inpatient and other health authority based-settings, with increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a wide range of therapeutic areas. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 473.title: Selected Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHRM 473.description: Diverse pharmacy practice experiences in various pharmacy practice, research, health policy, education, and other settings. Placement options will vary from year to year depending on practicum site availability. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 481.title: Healthcare Quality Improvement
PHRM 481.description: Builds on the foundation of patient care and management learning with knowledge about healthcare system improvement. Focuses on principles of quality measurement and quality improvement in health. Pass/Fail.

PHRM 491.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient
PHRM 491.description: Application of integrated problem-solving skills to resolve increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a variety of outpatient settings. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 491.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 492.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Inpatient and Health Authority-Based
PHRM 492.description: Application of integrated problem-solving skills to resolve increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a variety of inpatient and/or health authority-based settings. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 492.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 493.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Specialized Outpatient
PHRM 493.description: Application of integrated problem-solving skills to resolve increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a variety of specialized outpatient settings.
PHRM 493.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 494.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Ambulatory/Primary Care
PHRM 494.description: Application of integrated problem-solving skills to resolve increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in a variety of ambulatory or primary care settings. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 494.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 495.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Selected Direct Patient Care
PHRM 495.description: Application of integrated problem-solving skills to resolve increasingly complex drug-therapy problems in outpatient or inpatient settings. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 495.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 496.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience - Selected Direct Patient Care or Non-Direct Patient Care
PHRM 496.description: Options available in such domains as patient care (various settings), research, health policy, education, and others. The available placement options will vary from year to year depending on site/practice educator availability. Pass/Fail.
PHRM 496.prerequisiteText: All of PHRM_V 451, PHRM_V 452, PHRM_V 453, PHRM_V 461

PHRM 499.title: Comprehensive Examination
PHRM 499.description: Assessment of skills in the clinical problem-solving process. Pass/Fail.
